name: AI Now Institute
what: AI Now Institute is an independent research institute producing policy research on AI's social consequences, corporate power, surveillance and public accountability.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://ainowinstitute.org/publications/double-agents; activity also at https://ainowinstitute.org/news/palantir-hires-a-former-democratic-senator-as-it-faces-scrutiny-in-new-congress (verified 2026-11-10).

name: AI Objectives Institute
what: AI Objectives Institute is a non-profit research and development lab working on how AI and economic systems can reflect human objectives. Its team builds tools and conducts research on AI governance, markets and structural risks.
source: website: https://ai.objectives.institute/ and https://ai.objectives.institute/team (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "the Institute is a non-profit research lab working to ensure that both AI and future economic systems are built and deployed with genuine human objectives at their core" and "Our team builds tools and develops research".

name: AI Risk and Vulnerability Alliance
what: AI Risk and Vulnerability Alliance is a non-profit that runs AVID, a database and toolset for reporting and managing vulnerabilities in AI systems. It works with volunteer engineers and researchers to document AI failure modes and support risk management.
source: website: https://avidml.org/arva/ and https://avidml.org/community/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "AVID is the flagship effort of the non-profit organization AI Risk and Vulnerability Alliance (ARVA)" and "We build tools for practitioners and communities to interrogate the growing number of models capable of producing material harm to our world". github and linkedin_org: linked from https://avidml.org/arva/. community_url and events_url: linked from https://avidml.org/community/. takes_contributors: the community page invites volunteer engineers to join Discord, submit reports and open pull requests.

name: Air Alliance Houston
what: Air Alliance Houston is a non-profit advocacy organization working to reduce the public health impacts of air pollution and advance environmental justice in Houston. It runs AirMail, a system that scans state air permit applications and notifies nearby residents, and publishes air monitoring and pollution data.
source: website: https://airalliancehouston.org/ and https://airalliancehouston.org/updates/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Air Alliance Houston is a non-profit advocacy organization working to reduce the public health impacts from air pollution and advance environmental justice" and "AirMail is Air Alliance Houston’s new real-time public notification system for air permit applications". linkedin_org and careers_url: linked from https://airalliancehouston.org/. events_url: linked from https://airalliancehouston.org/updates/.

name: Airbnb.org
what: Airbnb.org is a non-profit that provides free emergency housing to people affected by disasters, illness or other crises. It works with partner organizations and uses Airbnb's platform and host network to arrange short-term stays.
source: website: https://www.airbnb.org/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Free emergency housing for neighbours in need" and "Airbnb.org is a non-profit founded by Airbnb" and "powered by Airbnb’s technology". takes_contributors: the homepage offers host support through its "Support as a host" link.

name: Alliance of Civic Technologists
what: Alliance of Civic Technologists is a decentralized network of volunteer civic technology organizations across the United States. It connects local groups so they can share learning, support each other and improve how governments use technology and deliver public services.
source: website: https://www.civictechnologists.org/ and https://www.civictechnologists.org/join (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "ACT is a decentralized network of civic tech volunteer organizations" and "support, grow, and enable a network of local volunteer civic technology organizations". linkedin_org and community_url: linked from https://www.civictechnologists.org/. takes_contributors: https://www.civictechnologists.org/join lists joining a local organization, starting a chapter and joining Discord.

name: American Foundation for the Blind
what: The American Foundation for the Blind is a US nonprofit expanding opportunities for people who are blind or have low vision through advocacy, research, accessible technology and professional services. It was founded in 1921.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.afb.org/research-and-initiatives/ai-series/ai-quagmire (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Aquaya
what: Aquaya is a nonprofit research and consulting organization that works to improve water, sanitation and hygiene access in low- and middle-income countries. It collects and analyzes WASH data and builds tools to inform policy, programme and financing decisions.
source: website: https://aquaya.org/ and https://aquaya.org/careers/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Aquaya is a nonprofit research and consulting organization dedicated to advancing global health through universal access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH)" and "Aquaya translates data into knowledge into action". linkedin_org and careers_url: linked from https://aquaya.org/.

name: Awana Digital
what: Awana Digital is a non-profit that works with Indigenous and frontline communities to build technology for defending land, culture and human rights. Its tools include CoMapeo for territory monitoring and mapping, Terrastories for place-based storytelling and the Earth Defenders Toolkit.
source: website: https://awana.digital/ and https://awana.digital/get-involved (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Awana Digital is a non-profit building decentralized technology hand-in-hand with Indigenous partners" and "We partner with earth defenders to co-develop technology for social justice". linkedin_org and community_url: linked from https://awana.digital/. careers_url: linked from https://awana.digital/. takes_contributors: the Get Involved page lists developer roles, fellowships and a public Discord channel.

name: Ballotpedia
what: Ballotpedia is a non-profit digital encyclopedia of American politics covering elections, candidates, offices and ballot measures. It has 758,643 encyclopedic articles and says it has had more than 1.2 billion page views since 2007.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/10/30/elections-ballotpedia-is-covering-in-november-2026/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Beeck Center for Social Impact and Innovation
what: Beeck Center for Social Impact and Innovation is the Beeck Center for Social Impact and Innovation at Georgetown University works to build a people-centred, digitally enabled government, connecting government and the civic tech ecosystem through research, networks and practical tools. It was founded in 2014.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://beeckcenter.georgetown.edu/governments-are-counting-ai-tools-they-should-be-measuring-public-value/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Benetech
what: Benetech is a nonprofit building accessible education technology, including Bookshare and its Global Certified Accessible programme. It campaigns to make accessibility the norm in schools and institutions.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://benetech.org/csun-2026-accessibility-ai-title-ii-benetech/; activity also at https://benetech.org/blog/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Berkeley Institute for Data Science
what: Berkeley Institute for Data Science is a research institute at UC Berkeley that supports data-intensive research, open-source software and data science training. It runs programs in open scholarship, AI and science, and hosts events and training for researchers across disciplines.
source: website: https://bids.berkeley.edu/ and https://bids.berkeley.edu/about (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "BIDS is a home for data-intensive research, open-source software, & data science training programs" and "BIDS contributes to a number of open source, open science, and open data resource communities in support of academic research". founding_year: "Since its launch in 2013, BIDS has cultivated an environment of open inquiry and discovery". linkedin_org and events_url: linked from https://bids.berkeley.edu/.

name: Berkman Klein Center for the Internet and Society
what: The Berkman Klein Center for the Internet and Society is an academic research center at Harvard University that studies the internet and digital society. It builds tools and platforms and runs fellowships and public programs on the internet, law and digital policy.
source: what from https://cyber.harvard.edu/about (accessed 2026-11-10): "We are a research center, premised on the observation that what we seek to learn is not already recorded." and "We design. We code. We construct." website from https://cyber.harvard.edu/; github linked from the about page at https://github.com/berkmancenter; linkedin_org linked from the events page at https://www.linkedin.com/company/berkman-center-for-internet-&-society-at-harvard-university; events_url linked from the home page at https://cyber.harvard.edu/events.

name: BetaNYC
what: BetaNYC is a New York City nonprofit that helps residents use civic technology, open data and design to improve their neighborhoods. It runs public programs, a data help desk and civic tools including Boundaries Map and the Urban Heat Portal.
source: what from https://www.beta.nyc/about/ (accessed 2026-11-10): "BetaNYC is a civic organization dedicated to improving lives in New York through civic design, technology, and data." founding_year from the same page: "BetaNYC began in 2008 as the NYC Open Government meetup". website from https://www.beta.nyc/; linkedin_org linked from the home page at https://www.linkedin.com/company/betanyc/; events_url linked from the home page at https://www.beta.nyc/events/; careers_url linked from the home page at https://www.beta.nyc/our-work/get-involved/.

name: BillBoard
what: BillBoard is a Maryland nonprofit that tracks US Congress legislation and publishes nonpartisan, source-linked explanations of bills, hearings and official actions. It provides reporting and tools intended to help everyday voters understand what legislation would do and who it could affect.
source: what from https://mybillboard.org/about (accessed 2026-11-10): "BillBoard is a Maryland nonprofit building nonpartisan, source-linked public understanding of legislation." and "Our public newsroom is designed for everyday voters." website from https://mybillboard.org/.

name: Boston Area Research Initiative (BARI)
what: The Boston Area Research Initiative is a research center at Northeastern University that uses civic data and community research partnerships to study social, economic and environmental issues in Greater Boston. It runs the Boston Data Portal and convenes researchers, public agencies and community groups.
source: what from https://cssh.northeastern.edu/bari/about/ (accessed 2026-11-10): "BARI pursues civically engaged research that leverages data to advance social, economic, and environmental justice in collaboration with the communities of greater Boston." website from https://cssh.northeastern.edu/bari/; events_url linked from the home page at https://cssh.northeastern.edu/events/.

name: California Department of Technology (CDT)
what: The California Department of Technology is the state's central information technology agency. It oversees statewide IT policy, project delivery and security, and provides shared infrastructure and digital services to state government.
source: what from https://www.cdt.ca.gov/about/ (accessed 2026-11-10): "The California Department of Technology leads the state’s drive to deliver clear, fast, dependable, and equitable public services." website from https://www.cdt.ca.gov/; linkedin_org and careers_url linked from the home page at https://www.linkedin.com/company/california-department-of-technology and https://www.cdt.ca.gov/career-opportunities/.

name: California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA)
what: The California Privacy Protection Agency is the state agency that implements and enforces California's consumer privacy law. It operates the Delete Request and Opt-out Platform and a data broker registry, and educates the public about privacy rights.
source: what from https://cppa.ca.gov/about_us/jobs.html (accessed 2026-11-10): "CalPrivacy is the first of its kind agency in the US created to protect the consumer privacy of Californians." and "We implement the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), enforce its regulations, and educate the public about their rights and obligations under the law." website from https://cppa.ca.gov/; careers_url linked from the home page at https://cppa.ca.gov/about_us/jobs.html.

name: CarbonPlan
what: CarbonPlan is a non-profit that analyses climate solutions, focusing on carbon offsets, carbon removal, and climate risk. It publishes open data and tools including OffsetsDB and Open Climate Risk.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://carbonplan.org/blog/pnw-wildfires-2026 (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Center for AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP)
what: The Center for AI and Digital Policy is a global nonprofit based in Washington, DC that works on AI governance grounded in democratic values, human rights and the rule of law. It publishes an annual AI policy index and runs a policy clinic, fellows program and public events.
source: what from https://www.caidp.org/about-2/ (accessed 2026-11-10): "Founded in Washington, DC, CAIDP is a global nonprofit dedicated to AI governance grounded in democratic values, human rights, and the rule of law." website from https://www.caidp.org/; events_url linked from the home page at https://www.caidp.org/events/.

name: Center for Civic Design
what: Center for Civic Design is an US non-profit that applies plain language, accessibility, information design and research to election materials and voter journeys. It publishes free tools, field guides and research for election officials.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://civicdesign.org/tools/election-home-stretch/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Center for Digital Democracy
what: The Center for Digital Democracy is a research and advocacy organization that works on digital privacy, consumer protection and the accountability of technology platforms. Its work covers digital marketing, data practices and the effects of technology on young people and democratic processes.
source: what from https://democraticmedia.org/about (accessed 2026-11-10): "CDD works to protect and expand digital rights and data justice through research-led initiatives designed to influence policymakers, corporate leaders, the news media, civil society, and the general public." website from https://democraticmedia.org/.

name: Center for Informed Democracy and Social Cyber-Security (IDeaS)
what: The Center for Informed Democracy and Social Cyber-Security is a Carnegie Mellon University research center that studies disinformation, hate speech and extremism online. It runs research, education and community programs intended to help people understand and resist online manipulation.
source: what from https://www.cmu.edu/ideas-social-cybersecurity/ (accessed 2026-11-10): "CMU's center for the study of disinformation, hate speech and extremism online". founding_year from the same page (accessed 2026-11-10): "Read the NEXT Pittsburgh article on the launch of the IDeaS Center in 2019". website from https://www.cmu.edu/ideas-social-cybersecurity/; linkedin_org and events_url linked from the same page; region from the page footer address, "Pittsburgh, PA 15213".

name: Center for Tech and Civic Life
what: Center for Tech and Civic Life (CTCL) is a nonpartisan nonprofit modernising US election administration through grants, research, training and data tools. Its projects include the Ballot Information Project and Governance Project.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.techandciviclife.org/advancing-research-on-mid-level-election-office-staff/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: CivAI
what: CivAI is a nonprofit that educates the public about the capabilities and dangers of AI through interactive software demonstrations. It also gives briefings to government and civil society groups.
source: what and founding_year from https://civai.org/about (accessed 2026-11-10): "CivAI is a non-profit that educates the public about AI's capabilities and dangers using live software demonstrations." and "Since its founding in 2023". website from https://civai.org/; linkedin_org linked from https://civai.org/; careers_url linked from https://civai.org/ and https://civai.org/jobs.

name: Civic Data Atlas
what: Civic Data Atlas publishes Census demographic profiles for city council districts and neighborhoods in Chicago, New York City and Los Angeles. It is intended to help local officials, advocacy groups, journalists and residents understand who lives in each area.
source: what from https://civicdataatlas.org/about (accessed 2026-11-10): "Civic Data Atlas brings comprehensive demographic data to the two geographies that structure city life" and "It can help elected officials better understand their constituents and advocate for their interests." Cities are listed on https://civicdataatlas.org/. website from https://civicdataatlas.org/.

name: Civic Infrastructure Collaborative
what: Civic Infrastructure Collaborative is a Chicago nonprofit that works with public, private and civic partners on technology-enabled urban infrastructure projects. Its projects include electric vehicle charging, sensors and analytics for stormwater management, and capacity management in shared spaces.
source: what from https://www.infrastructureforward.org/about (accessed 2026-11-10): "CINCO's mission is to drive public value from core urban infrastructure through collaboration and technology-enabled innovation." Project examples are described on the same page. website from https://www.infrastructureforward.org/; linkedin_org linked from https://www.infrastructureforward.org/about.

name: Clooney Foundation for Justice
what: The Clooney Foundation for Justice runs TrialWatch, a program that trains people to monitor trials and document whether courts meet international fair-trial standards. Its online training platform covers courtroom conduct, the right to a lawyer and trial delays.
source: name, what and website from https://www.trialwatchtraining.org/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "This training program teaches the basics of how to be a trial monitor" and "It gathers all of the relevant international standards on what constitutes a fair trial." region from the candidate HQ recorded as USA in the batch file.

name: Code for America
what: Code for America is a US civic-tech nonprofit that works with governments to make public benefits and services easier to access, including SNAP, tax credits and criminal record relief.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://codeforamerica.org/news/anthropic-partnership/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Code for BTV
what: Code for BTV is a civic technology organization in Burlington, Vermont, that works with government and community partners on civic software and open data projects. It organizes volunteers to design, build and deliver tools for social and civic justice organizations across Vermont.
source: website: https://codeforbtv.org/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Code for BTV is a local civic technology organization based in Burlington, VT (USA)" and "We pull together teams of volunteers that build new tools for social and civic justice organizations". github: linked from https://codeforbtv.org/ and https://codeforbtv.org/contact/. events_url: linked from https://codeforbtv.org/. takes_contributors: the homepage says "Get involved!" and the contact page says "everyone is encouraged to join".

name: Code for Nashville
what: Code for Nashville is a volunteer Code for America brigade that works with community groups and Metro Nashville government to promote open data and build civic apps. Its projects include criminal record expungement tools, jail population reports and an online power of attorney form for immigrants.
source: website: https://www.codefornashville.org/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Code for Nashville is Nashville, Tennessee's Code for America Brigade" and "We are volunteers who collaborate with community groups (including activists, nonprofits, and government) to promote open data and build civic apps". github: linked from https://www.codefornashville.org/. takes_contributors: the page says "We are a growing organization and need members" and "The best way to become involved is to attend our next hack night".

name: Code for Science & Society
what: Code for Science & Society is a US public charity and fiscal sponsor for public-interest technology, data and research projects. It provides financial, operational and strategic support to open-source and open-data initiatives.
source: website: https://www.codeforsociety.org/ and https://www.codeforsociety.org/about (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Code for Science and Society is a registered US public charity" and "We promote technology initiatives that are equitable, open-source, and sustainable to advance global access to information." founding_year: "Since 2016, CS&S has built programs and united projects aligned with our mission". region from the Portland, OR address on https://www.codeforsociety.org/about. github and linkedin_org: linked from https://www.codeforsociety.org/ and https://www.codeforsociety.org/about. careers_url: linked from https://www.codeforsociety.org/ and https://www.codeforsociety.org/get-involved.

name: CodeAI
what: CodeAI is an education nonprofit, formerly Code.org, working so every K-12 student can learn AI and computer science. It provides free curriculum, teacher training and policy work, and says it has reached 155 million students and 3 million teachers in 190 countries.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.transformmagazine.net/articles/2026/codeorg-rebrand-encourages-critical-thinking-about-ai-technology/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Coding it Forward
what: Coding it Forward is a nonprofit that builds civic tech career paths for early-career technologists and places them in government agencies and nonprofits through its Fellowship.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.codingitforward.com/s/DC-Department-of-Human-Services-Fellow-Report.pdf; activity also at https://www.codingitforward.com/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Common Good AI
what: Common Good AI is a nonprofit that uses AI and digital tools to help communities deliberate, identify shared priorities and make collective decisions. It runs participatory projects, including a multi-state Forum and a WhatsApp chatbot pilot for community needs assessment.
source: website: https://commongoodai.org/ and https://commongoodai.org/mission (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Common Good AI is a non-profit organization that leverages human abilities to innovate and find solutions by integrating digital AI tools" and "We help communities tackle hard problems and collaborate at scale using pro-social digital tools and deliberative processes". region from the address "223 Bedford Avenue #A1002 Brooklyn, NY 11211" on https://commongoodai.org/contact. linkedin_org: linked from https://commongoodai.org/.

name: Community Data Science Collective
what: The Community Data Science Collective is an interdisciplinary research group of faculty and students at several US universities who study online communities and collaborative production. Its members use quantitative and qualitative methods to examine how communication and information technologies shape participation and public goods.
source: website: https://wiki.communitydata.science/Main_Page and https://wiki.communitydata.science/About (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "The Community Data Science Collective (CDSC) is an interdisciplinary research group made up of faculty and students" and "We are social scientists and computer scientists applying a range of quantitative and qualitative methods to the study of online communities". region from the candidate HQ Seattle in the batch file. takes_contributors: the About page says "we welcome anyone to join and participate in our group" and the Join CDSC page says "We are always looking for people who want to join the Community Data Science Collective".

name: Community Solutions
what: Community Solutions is a nonprofit working with more than 150 cities and counties through Built for Zero to reduce homelessness using real-time data and coordinated action.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://community.solutions/research-posts/2026-overall-homelessness-estimates/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: ConsiliumBots
what: ConsiliumBots is a nonprofit that builds virtual assistants and personalized recommendations from government data. Its tools help people make decisions about education, housing, and public benefits.
source: https://www.consiliumbots.com/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Our nonprofit organization is dedicated to leveraging technology to connect government data with the community in order to help people make better-informed decisions that can positively impact their well-being." linkedin_org linked from this page. Region from https://www.consiliumbots.com/contact/ ("New Haven 102 Audubon Street").

name: Convocation Research and Design Labs
what: Convocation Research and Design Labs is a research and design lab that studies security technology and protects people and organizations facing harassment, surveillance, and disinformation. It works with human rights groups, journalists, and nonprofits.
source: https://www.convocation.design/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "We protect people and organizations navigating hostile digital spaces. Privacy and security are human rights."

name: Cosmik
what: Cosmik builds open tools and networks for collective sensemaking, including a social knowledge network for researchers. It uses AI and decentralized publishing protocols such as ATProto to make research contributions discoverable and reusable.
source: https://cosmik.network/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Cosmik is helping create the research networks to support this future: open, collaborative, and built for rapid feedback and iteration." github and community_url linked from this page ("Github", "Cosmik Discord"); takes_contributors from the get-involved form linked on this page.

name: Creative Commons
what: Creative Commons is an international nonprofit that provides legal and technical tools for sharing knowledge and culture. Its licenses and public domain tools are used by Wikipedia, Flickr, and millions of other creators and institutions.
source: https://creativecommons.org/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "Creative Commons is an international nonprofit organization dedicated to defending and nurturing a commons of shared knowledge and culture that powers human creativity, equity, and innovation." linkedin_org and events_url linked from this page. takes_contributors from https://creativecommons.org/community/ ("There are a number of ways you can contribute your time to the open movement").

name: Crisis Text Line
what: Crisis Text Line provides free, 24-hour, confidential text support for people in crisis. It says it has supported over 11 million conversations in the US since 2013.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.crisistextline.org/blog/2026/10/28/when-a-young-person-is-in-crisis-what-do-they-reach-for/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Current AI
what: Current AI is a global nonprofit partnership that funds and builds open, public-interest AI infrastructure. It brings governments, philanthropists, researchers, and grassroots builders together around the Paris Charter on AI in the Public Interest.
source: https://www.currentai.org/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "A non-profit bridging government, philanthropy and tech". founding_year: "Founded at the AI Action Summit in Paris in February 2025". linkedin_org linked from this page; careers_url from https://www.currentai.org/careers.

name: CyPurr Collective
what: CyPurr Collective is a grassroots group that runs beginner-friendly digital security workshops and cryptoparties in New York City. It publishes its training materials under an open license so others can reuse and adapt them.
source: https://cypurr.org/ (accessed 2026-11-10). what: "To educate the public on cybersecurity in an accessible and holistic way with fun cats." github linked from this page. founding_year: "Cypurr Collective, est 2016".

name: Data & Society Research Institute
what: Data & Society is an independent nonprofit research institute studying the social implications of data, automation and AI, producing research to ground public debate and technology policy.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://datasociety.net/news-events/new-project-from-data-society-will-turn-a-worker-lens-on-the-ai-economy/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Data Foundation
what: The Data Foundation is a non-profit policy research organisation that promotes open data and evidence-informed public policy. It conducts research, publishes analysis and convenes a coalition of data leaders.
source: what from https://datafoundation.org/about (accessed 2026-11-10): "The Data Foundation champions the use of open data and evidence-informed public policy to make democratic society better for everyone." Non-profit status from the same page: "The Data Foundation is a Washington, DC-based, non-profit, non-partisan organization." website from https://datafoundation.org/; linkedin_org and events_url linked from https://datafoundation.org/.

name: Data Friendly Space
what: Data Friendly Space provides digital tools and data analysis for social impact and humanitarian organisations. It builds generative-AI tools for crisis response, including its GANNET suite.
source: what from https://www.datafriendlyspace.org/ (accessed 2026-11-10): "DFS provides digital tools and actionable data for social impact organisations to just get things done." The same page says: "Data Friendly Space builds generative-AI tools for crisis response." website from https://www.datafriendlyspace.org/; linkedin_org and careers_url linked from https://www.datafriendlyspace.org/.

name: DataKind
what: DataKind works with social impact organisations to design data science and AI projects, and builds shared products such as its Beacon community data platform. It also runs the Data for Good movement and education initiatives.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.datakind.org/2026/06/17/introducing-beacon-a-new-platform-for-community-data-coordinated-action/; activity also at https://www.datakind.org/blog/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Democracy Works
what: Democracy Works is a non-partisan nonprofit that builds voter engagement and election data tools, including TurboVote, the Elections API, and the Voting Information Project.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.democracy.works/news/democracy-works-expands-partnership-with-anthropic-ahead-of-2026-midterm-elections (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Election.org
what: Election.org is a nonpartisan civic reference publishing source-linked records on US elections, candidates, elected officials, campaign finance and local government. It provides charts, downloads and documented data endpoints.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://election.org/data (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Electronic Frontier Foundation
what: Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is a nonprofit defending civil liberties in the digital world through litigation, policy analysis, grassroots activism and technology development.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2026/11/google-forcing-ai-students-bs (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Epoch AI
what: Epoch AI is a non-profit research institute studying the trajectory of artificial intelligence. It publishes independent data, benchmarks and analysis on AI capabilities, compute and impacts.
source: what from https://epoch.ai/about (accessed 2026-11-10): "Epoch AI is a data-first research nonprofit investigating the future of artificial intelligence." website from https://epoch.ai/; github, linkedin_org and careers_url linked from https://epoch.ai/.

name: EveryoneOn
what: EveryoneOn is a US digital inclusion nonprofit connecting under-resourced communities to affordable internet, computers and digital skills training, with place-based work in California and Milwaukee.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.everyoneon.org/s/Everyone-On-2025-Impact-Report.pdf; activity also at https://www.everyoneon.org/blog-posts/q3update (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Feeding America
what: Feeding America is the largest hunger-relief organisation in the United States, a national network of 250+ food banks, 20+ state associations and 60,000+ agency partners. It distributes food and advocates on hunger policy.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.feedingamerica.org/about-us/press-room/elevating-voices-insights-report-2026 (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Free Law Project
what: Free Law Project is a non-profit that uses software, data and advocacy to make legal information more accessible. It runs CourtListener, the RECAP archive and related tools for public access to court records.

what: USAFacts is a nonpartisan civic initiative founded by Steve Ballmer that turns government data into free articles, reports and tools; it is privately funded and takes no advertising or external donations.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://usafacts.org/reports/government-10-k/; activity also at https://usafacts.org/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Vote.org
what: Vote.org is a nonpartisan nonprofit using technology and outreach to help Americans register, check registration, request mail ballots and find voting information. It says it has helped more than 40 million people get election-ready.
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.vote.org/press-releases/ten-million/ (verified 2026-11-10).
